_meta.note: Intellectual lifecycle of economic thought modeled as five lifecycle phases: formation, consolidation, maturation, stress, and renewal. Each lifecycle phase spans multiple supply chain epochs.

lifecycle_definition: The intellectual lifecycle of an economic paradigm follows a predictable N-D-C arc: formation (D exceeds C, constraints define the new problem space), consolidation (D and C balance, high N emerges), maturation (C begins to exceed D, productive output peaks), stress (C overshoots D, sustainability falls), and renewal-or-collapse (N falls, new D emerges from the rubble of the old paradigm).

phases.parent_N: Practical exchange knowledge without systematic theory
phases.key_insight: Practical exchange tools are invented long before systematic economic theory. The C outputs of this lifecycle phase become the D constraints of the next.

phases.parent_N: State-managed commerce with emerging market theory
phases.key_insight: Systematic economic doctrine emerges. Mercantilism provides a coherent (if flawed) D framework. Classical political economy demolishes mercantilist D and creates high-C outputs that become the foundation for the next lifecycle phase.

phases.parent_N: Mathematical and institutional economics with policy tools
D_parameters: Labor value theory constraint (resolved by marginalism)
Classical Say's Law orthodoxy (resolved by Keynes)
phases.key_insight: Peak productive epoch. Two major paradigm revolutions (marginalism, Keynesianism) each generate very high C outputs. N is highest in this lifecycle phase. Balance is close to optimal. The institutional architecture built here (IMF, World Bank, national accounts) remains in place.

phases.parent_N: Monetarist rules and global financial integration
phases.key_insight: C begins to exceed D as financial engineering outpaces regulatory theory. The lifecycle phase is still coherent but sustainability is falling. The 2008 crisis is the endpoint of a C overshoot that built over 20 years.

An open transition phase where the old D has dissolved but no new D has fully crystallized. Multiple C streams are active. The Tholonic model predicts this phase ends when one candidate C stream becomes dominant enough to re-impose D constraints, instantiating a new child N. Climate macro or AI-augmented planning are the leading candidates.

system.interpretation: The intellectual lifecycle of economics is strongest during the period of mathematical and institutional maturation (1871-1973), where both constraint resolution and institutional output are high. The current open transition phase is a structural bottleneck: D has not reconstituted and C outputs are not converging. The Tholonic model suggests stability returns when a new dominant framework provides enough D to bound the proliferating C outputs into a coherent child N.
